name: Pago Florentino

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Cabernet Sauvignon, Sangiovese, Grenache, Carignan and Zinfandel fully without cooking off their freshness.
Tempranillo is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
